newsitem.title: USA: Aames Financial eyes U.K. expansion.
newsitem.headline: Aames Financial eyes U.K. expansion.

text.p: Aames Financial Corp is weighing an expansion into the United Kingdom, the company's senior vice president for finance said Wednesday in response to a question at a Piper Jaffray investment conference.
Mark Elbaum said the expansion could take the form of a start-up company, an acquisition, a merger or joint venture.
He said a possible joint venture partner has already been identified but he did not identify it.
Aames is a leading U.S. home-equity lender specializing in "C" and "D" class borrowers.

Elbaum said after his presentation he was comfortable with earnings estimates of $3.05 per share for the fiscal year ending in June 1997 and $3.90 per share for the year ending in June 1998. The estimates are those of Piper Jaffray analyst Jeffrey Evanson, who has a strong buy on Aames stock.
In fiscal 1996 Aames earned $2.09 per share.
The analyst said his bullish view is based on "loan growth origination."
Elbaum also said in response to a question that a recent Forbes magazine article critical of the company did not give a balanced view.

Elbaum said the company's loans may have higher delinquencies than those of some of its competitors, but he said the loss rate was a low 13 basis points recently and reserves were an ample 1.20 percentage point rate.
Elbaum said the company's home-equity loan product was primarily driven by consumer debt. "Debt consolidation is the number one reason people come to Aames," he said.
